pages.text: The sample burns completely in oxygen: q = m·ΔH_c. The bomb sits in water of heat capacity C = 10 kJ/K, which warms by ΔT = q/C. Too small a rise cannot be read well; too big and the water loses heat while it is read. The oxygen must be enough to burn all of it - each gram needs its own share.
$(thing)Set$(): Sample mass, Oxygen pressure.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Stirrer heat: the reading drifts by ±0.5%·d.
$(thing)Limits$(): The bomb is over its rated pressure.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): One burn at a time.
$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Heat released: q = m·ΔH_c$(br)Temperature rise: ΔT = q/C$(br)Burnt: p_O₂ / (demand · m)
